Do NOT run `--execute` or any live-LLM path. RTE_DISABLE_LIVE_LLM_IN_TESTS=1 stays set for every test/probe step.

For each of the 26 failures, classify the root cause as one of: (a) test has stale expectation against post-E7/E8/E9 design — repair the test; (b) production code drifted from the consensus design — repair the code; (c) genuine ambiguity in the spec — escalate via pal/consensus before choosing direction. Preserve the E3 contracts, E4 alias resolution, E7 cell-aliased ladders + per-request failover, E8 model_map v3, and E9 spend-optimizer/route-optimizer-metadata invariants. Test repairs must not re-anchor on legacy ladder constants or pre-E8 model strings.

The `--print-config` JSON contract change is operator-visible. Any addition to its schema must be recorded in docs/03-reference/repo-truth-extractor.md (or the equivalent operator-facing reference doc) within this packet's commit, not in a separate trailing PR.

Test-environment fixes (Cluster F / litellm) must repair the import boundary, not silently `pytest.importorskip` the affected tests. If skipping is the right call, it must be a documented, deferred decision with a follow-up TP.

STOP CONDITIONS — Codex must abort and surface to the operator if ANY of: (1) S1 F-VERIFY-001 ancestry/proof/ledger gate fails on origin/main; (2) SERIES_VERIFICATION_REPORT.md or TP-RTE-COSTPROFILE-F-VERIFY-001/PROOF.json is missing on origin/main, or PROOF.json fails to parse; (3) NOT_VERIFIED_ACCEPTED_AS_EVIDENCE is missing from the F-VERIFY-001 row of task-packets/INDEX.md on origin/main; (4) the S8 clean-checkout import probe fails under `PYTHONPATH=src` (the package uses an `src/` layout and is not installed at execution time, so a bare `python -c "import dopemux.cli"` is invalid as a gate); (5) any required verification pipeline in this packet fails when wrapped under `bash -o pipefail` (pytest|tee and run_extraction_v5.py|tee gates must surface upstream non-zero exits — masking is prohibited); (6) S2 selects a target_policy treatment (option ii or iii) that would break existing downstream consumers of `--print-config` without explicit operator approval recorded in REPAIR_DECISIONS.md. pr.title: fix(rte): cost-profile series full-suite repair (F-FULLSUITE-REPAIR)
pr.body:
## Summary
- Repairs the 26 RTE-suite failures observed under TP-RTE-COSTPROFILE-F-VERIFY-001 (status: NOT_VERIFIED_ACCEPTED_AS_EVIDENCE).
- Reconciles cost-profile route expectations across v3/v5 routing tests, pre-live gate defaults, route readiness summaries, pricing coverage, and promptpack D-step contract metadata.
- Adds `cost_profile` to the `--print-config` emitted JSON so the operator can see the resolved profile in the config surface (or, if the operator contract is changed to a different visibility surface, that change is recorded in docs/03-reference/repo-truth-extractor.md as part of this PR).
- Repairs non-cost-profile failures: prescan truthfulness/incremental semantics, reporting seam dependency contract, and `litellm` test-environment import.

## Scope
Repair-only against the failure inventory captured in F-VERIFY-001/SERIES_VERIFICATION_REPORT.md. No new features. No live LLM execution. No re-issue of the F verification gate (a follow-up F-VERIFY-002 packet handles that).

## Failure Clusters Addressed
- **Cluster A — Cost-profile routing drift (8 files):** test_intelligence_routing_integration.py, test_phase_d_contract_hardening.py, test_pre_live_gate_v25.py, test_promptpack_v1_v2.py, test_run_extraction_v3_model_routing.py, test_run_extraction_v5_benchmark_route_ownership.py, test_run_extraction_v5_live_readiness.py, test_run_extraction_v5_operator_safety.py.
- **Cluster B — Pricing coverage drift (2 files):** test_pricing_coverage.py, test_run_extraction_v5_cost_cap.py.
- **Cluster C — `--print-config` cost_profile emission (operator contract):** run_extraction_v5.py print_config builder + docs/03-reference/repo-truth-extractor.md.
- **Cluster D — Prescan truthfulness/incremental (4 files):** test_code_prescan_truthfulness.py, test_prescan_contracts.py, test_prescan_e2e_smoke.py, test_prescan_incremental.py.
- **Cluster E — Reporting seam deps contract (1 file):** test_reporting_seam.py.
- **Cluster F — litellm test-env import (1 file):** test_rte_v5_characterization.py + src/dopemux/cli.py.

## Validation
Full RTE suite under RTE_DISABLE_LIVE_LLM_IN_TESTS=1 returns exit 0 (or any residual non-zero is itemized per-failure in REPAIR_DECISIONS.md with traceability to an explicitly-deferred follow-up packet). `--print-config` JSON contains a `cost_profile` field. pal/codereview reports no critical findings on the repair diff. pal/precommit returns SAFE TO COMMIT.

## NOT_RUN
- Live LLM/provider calls.
- `--execute` bounded lane.
- F-VERIFY-002 series verification gate (separate packet).
- Cross-pipeline integration with v3-pipeline (separate authority).

## Residual Risks / UNKNOWNs
- Some failure clusters may turn out to span multiple authoritative sources (e.g., pre-live gate default could be a docs-vs-code conflict). pal/consensus is invoked in S2 to resolve ambiguity before any code/test edits, but a wrong call would land hidden behavior drift. REPAIR_DECISIONS.md captures every choice for audit.
- The `--print-config` schema change is operator-visible. Tools that parse this output (e.g., CI scrapers, dashboard probes) may need a coordinated bump. Documented in docs change.
- litellm test-env repair direction (defensive import vs. test-fixture install vs. requirements-tightening) is decided at S8; the wrong direction risks masking a real production import gap.

@codex review

steps.task: Preflight (F-VERIFY-001 mainline-ancestry / proof-ledger gate). Also capture the stacked-ancestry caveat (E3/E4/E7/E8/E9) for reproducibility. STOP CONDITIONS — abort execution and surface to operator if ANY of: (a) F-VERIFY-001 proof/ledger ancestry check fails; (b) SERIES_VERIFICATION_REPORT.md or TP-RTE-COSTPROFILE-F-VERIFY-001/PROOF.json is absent on origin/main; (c) PROOF.json fails to parse; (d) NOT_VERIFIED_ACCEPTED_AS_EVIDENCE is missing from the INDEX row; (e) any required-pipeline check anywhere in this packet fails (these are now wrapped with `bash -o pipefail` so upstream failures are no longer masked by tee); (f) the clean-checkout import probe in S8 fails under `PYTHONPATH=src` (the package uses an `src/` layout, so a bare `python -c "import dopemux.cli"` is not a valid gate). steps.task: Root-cause classification with PAL analyze + thinkdeep + consensus. For each of the 26 observed failures (inventory frozen from F-VERIFY-001's SERIES_VERIFICATION_REPORT.md), classify as: (a) test has stale expectation — repair the test; (b) code drifted from consensus design — repair the code; (c) ambiguous — pal/consensus before deciding. Do NOT edit any code or tests in this step. EXPLICIT DECISION REQUIRED: how do `target_policy` (legacy routing-policy field; F-VERIFY-001 observed it emitting `balanced_openrouter`) and the new `cost_profile` field coexist in `--print-config`? Pick one of: (i) both fields emitted, `target_policy` deprecated with a notice; (ii) `cost_profile` supersedes `target_policy`, removing the latter (operator-breaking — requires migration note); (iii) `target_policy` removed in favor of `cost_profile` only. Record the decision + rationale in REPAIR_DECISIONS.md and propagate to S5.
validation: REPAIR_DECISIONS.md exists with all 26 failures classified.
Each classification names an authoritative source (E-series packet ID, file path, or consensus decision ID).
Any (c) ambiguity entry has a recorded pal/consensus outcome before S3+ proceed.

steps.task: Cluster A — Cost-profile routing reconciliation. Apply the S2-classified repair direction across the 8 failing files: test_intelligence_routing_integration.py (gpt-4o vs gpt-5.4-mini), test_phase_d_contract_hardening.py (D-step Gemini vs OpenRouter), test_pre_live_gate_v25.py (balanced_openrouter vs cost), test_promptpack_v1_v2.py (D0/D1 Gemini vs OpenRouter), test_run_extraction_v3_model_routing.py (3 route contract/strict/fallback expectations), test_run_extraction_v5_benchmark_route_ownership.py (H3 OpenRouter strict override), test_run_extraction_v5_live_readiness.py (benchmark-owned route readiness scope), test_run_extraction_v5_operator_safety.py (doctor/preflight exit 2 + route readiness + strict override). If the consensus during S2 was to expose this via a different visibility surface (e.g., a dedicated --print-cost-profile subcommand), implement that surface instead and update tests + docs accordingly. Investigate: does the test fixture mock `sys.modules` in a way that breaks litellm's import chain? Is the litellm import in src/dopemux/cli.py at module-load time when it should be lazy?
